+-- 089_source_type_vocabulary.sql
+--
+-- THE COLUMN DECLARES ITS OWN VOCABULARY, SO THE WRITER CAN REFUSE A BAD VALUE.
+--
+-- WHAT WENT WRONG, MEASURED ON THE BATCH THAT WROTE THIS. A session admitted a source
+-- with source_type = 'journal-article', copied from Crossref's `type` field. The value
+-- this project uses is 'journal_article', with an underscore. Three things then failed
+-- in sequence, and each is a mechanism rather than an oversight:
+--
+--   1. `db.py add-source` ACCEPTED IT. Every other vocabulary-bearing flag on that
+--      command validates against the live schema -- their help strings literally read
+--      "Live vocabulary, read from the column's own CHECK" -- because `dbcore.check_values`
+--      reads the column's CHECK and `check_declared` refuses anything outside it. That
+--      guard was silently OFF here for one reason: the column declared no CHECK, and an
+--      empty vocabulary reads as NO CONSTRAINT.
+--
+--   2. `add-source --help` ADVERTISED THE WRONG VALUE. Its text read
+--      "journal-article | report | book | thesis | standard" -- the hyphen -- so the tool
+--      told the operator to write the value its own blocking check rejects.
+--
+--   3. test_db_integrity B05 CAUGHT IT FROM A HAND-CURATED TUPLE. `VALID_ST` is a
+--      seventeen-value tuple maintained in the test file, which is CLAUDE.md rule 8's
+--      named anti-pattern: "a list maintained alongside the thing it describes, where
+--      the list and the thing drift and only the list is checked." The same file already
+--      fixed exactly this for `gaps.status` one check along (B06, 2026-09-18) by reading
+--      `dbcore.check_expression` instead of a tuple -- and the comment recording that fix
+--      sits eleven lines below the tuple this migration retires.
+--
+-- WHY THE FIX IS HERE AND NOT IN A PYTHON ENUM. CLAUDE.md section 4 is explicit:
+-- "Vocabularies come from the schema, not a list in code." There is no SourceType enum in
+-- schemas/enums.py and this migration deliberately does not add one -- that would move the
+-- list, not remove it, and would leave two homes where rule 5 allows one. With the CHECK in
+-- place the schema is the single home and three consumers derive from it: the writer's
+-- refusal, the writer's help text, and B05's assertion.
+--
+-- THE VOCABULARY IS TRANSCRIBED FROM `VALID_ST` UNCHANGED, deliberately. Seventeen values,
+-- including 'code', which D-0157 section 4.6 ratified. Widening or narrowing it here would
+-- bury a doctrinal change inside a mechanical one; the set moves only by a later migration
+-- that argues for the move. Two rows carry a non-NULL source_type at the time of writing
+-- ('report' and 'journal_article'), both already inside the set, so this constrains future
+-- writes and invalidates nothing on disk.
+--
+-- NULL REMAINS LEGAL. 25 of 27 rows have no source_type, and requiring one would turn a
+-- forward-looking constraint into a backlog. The CHECK reads `IS NULL OR IN (...)`, which
+-- is the shape `dbcore.check_values` is taught to parse.
+--
+-- AFTER_DATA: 20260920033222
+--
+-- REBUILD, because SQLite cannot add a CHECK to an existing column. The table DDL below was
+-- GENERATED from the live schema rather than retyped -- 97 columns is exactly the kind of
+-- hand-transcription that introduces the defect it is meant to fix -- with only the
+-- source_type line altered. No trigger exists on this table. The one non-auto index is
+-- recreated below. THE FIVE DEPENDENT VIEWS ARE DROPPED AND RECREATED VERBATIM, and the
+-- first attempt at this migration proved why: SQLite validates the WHOLE schema during
+-- ALTER TABLE ... RENAME, so a view left pointing at the dropped name aborts the rename
+-- with 'error in view v_evidence_authors: no such table'. It rolled back atomically and
+-- left the blob untouched, which is migrate_db.py's F5 transaction boundary doing its job.
+-- Their definitions are UNCHANGED -- captured from the live schema and re-emitted as they
+-- stood, not rewritten -- so this is a drop-and-restore, not a redefinition.
+
+-- Views first: see the note above.
+DROP VIEW IF EXISTS v_determination_provenance;
+DROP VIEW IF EXISTS v_evidence_authors;
+DROP VIEW IF EXISTS v_item_provenance;
+DROP VIEW IF EXISTS v_source_admission;
+DROP VIEW IF EXISTS v_source_reach_all;
+

+-- 090_root_claim_without_a_root.sql
+--
+-- A ROW THAT CLAIMS A PRIMARY MEASUREMENT AND NAMES NO ROOT IS THE ONE CASE THE ROOT
+-- VIEW COULD NOT SEE.
+--
+-- WHAT WENT WRONG, MEASURED ON THE BATCH THAT WROTE THIS. Batch 19 wrote extraction 57
+-- with root_type='measurement_primary', root_ref_id NULL and root_id NULL: a value
+-- REF-01005 did not measure (it tested 1:12, 1:16 and 1:20 only), attributed to a 1957
+-- dissertation this corpus does not hold. The prose in root_classification_basis said so
+-- honestly. THE TYPED COLUMNS SAID "a primary measurement whose root is nothing", and no
+-- gate could contradict them.
+--
+-- `v_unregistered_roots` exists for exactly this -- a root held outside the corpus -- and
+-- its WHERE opened `sve.root_id IS NOT NULL`. So it examines rows that NAME an external
+-- root and are missing its registry entry, and it is blind to the strictly worse case:
+-- a row that names no root at all. `v_value_independence` drops the same rows from
+-- independent_root_count silently. The blind spot was named in db.py's own comment when
+-- root_type was made amendable, and making the repair path is not the same as closing it:
+-- the next `add-extraction --root-type measurement_primary` with both columns null is
+-- still invisible.
+--
+-- WHAT THIS CHANGES. The view keeps its existing subject and gains the missing one, with
+-- a `defect` column saying which case each row is, because they are not the same problem
+-- and a reader fixing them needs to know:
+--
+--   'unregistered'  -- names an external root_id with no external_root_registry entry.
+--                      The original subject, unchanged.
+--   'rootless'      -- claims a rooted root_type and names NO root at all, by either
+--                      column. Nothing to register and nothing to point at.
+--
+-- 'untraced' is deliberately NOT a defect. It is the vocabulary's own word for "the root
+-- is not known", so a row that says untraced and names nothing is consistent, which is
+-- exactly what extraction 57 was corrected TO. The rooted types are the three that assert
+-- a provenance a reader could in principle follow.
+--
+-- NO DATA CHANGES. This is a view definition only; the one row that provoked it was
+-- already corrected to 'untraced' by data_20260920041301. The view is expected to render
+-- 0 rows immediately after this migration, and that is a real 0 rather than a vacuous
+-- one -- CLAUDE.md rule 4's "treat a 0-row object as unproven, not clean" applies, so the
+-- falsifier is stated here: write an extraction with root_type='measurement_primary' and
+-- no root and it must appear.
+--
+-- AFTER_DATA: 20260920041301
+
+DROP VIEW IF EXISTS v_unregistered_roots;
+
+CREATE VIEW v_unregistered_roots AS
+    SELECT sve.extraction_id,
+           sve.slug,
+           sve.parameter_id,
+           t.canonical_en AS parameter_label,
+           sve.root_id,
+           'unregistered' AS defect
+    FROM source_value_extractions sve
+    JOIN base_parameters p ON p.parameter_id = sve.parameter_id
+    JOIN terms t           ON t.term_id      = p.term_id
+    WHERE sve.root_id IS NOT NULL
+      AND sve.root_ref_id IS NULL
+      AND NOT EXISTS (
+          SELECT 1 FROM external_root_registry err
+          WHERE err.root_id = sve.root_id)
+
+    UNION ALL
+
+    SELECT sve.extraction_id,
+           sve.slug,
+           sve.parameter_id,
+           t.canonical_en AS parameter_label,
+           sve.root_id,
+           'rootless' AS defect
+    FROM source_value_extractions sve
+    JOIN base_parameters p ON p.parameter_id = sve.parameter_id
+    JOIN terms t           ON t.term_id      = p.term_id
+    WHERE sve.root_id IS NULL
+      AND sve.root_ref_id IS NULL
+      AND sve.root_type IN ('measurement_primary', 'participatory_finding',
+                            'committee_assertion');
+
+PRAGMA user_version = 90;

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Render a page of a persisted PDF to an image, so a session can LOOK at the scan.
+
+WHY THIS EXISTS, AND IT IS A DEFECT REPORT ON BATCH 19 RATHER THAN A FEATURE NOTE.
+
+Batch 19 mined REF-01005's bibliography out of a scanned 1979 microfiche. The PDF's OCR
+text layer is badly damaged, so the batch:
+
+  * recorded "no OCR engine is available in this environment (no tesseract, no
+    pdftotext), so this text layer is the best that exists here";
+  * transcribed 38 entries with per-entry damage flags, marking authors "illegible" and
+    years "not resolvable";
+  * built a floor/ceiling BAND into scripts/research/mining_screen.py to bound how much
+    the damage might be hiding;
+  * and wrote all of that into a session record, an attestation, three candidates, two
+    extractions and an amendment to a filed gap.
+
+EVERY ONE OF THOSE CLAIMS WAS WRONG, AND THE DOCUMENT WAS LEGIBLE THE WHOLE TIME. The
+pages are JBIG2 images inside the PDF. Rendering one and looking at it takes a second and
+reads plainly: "Templer, J.A. Stair shape and human movement, Unpublished doctoral
+dissertation. New York: Columbia University, 1974." -- transcribed by the batch as
+"[?] [Un]iversity". "Walter, F. ... Disabled Living Foundation, 1971." -- the batch called
+the initial unexplained and the year unreadable, and built a candidate trail on it.
+
+THE MISTAKE WAS NOT THE BAD TRANSCRIPTION. It was reasoning about the LIMITS OF A TEXT

===== GAP-013
FOUR DEEPER FIXES A /simplify PASS NAMED AND THIS SESSION DID NOT TAKE, each wider than the diff it reviewed. (1) _AMENDABLE and _CORRECTABLE are hand-curated tuples in db.py -- the 'list maintained alongside the thing it describes' rule 8 forbids, and rule 8 already names amend-source as an outstanding violator. This session GREW _AMENDABLE by one (jurisdiction) rather than deriving it. The named fix: declare the provenance class on the field in schemas/evidence_source.py (json_schema_extra={'provenance':'judgement'}) and have both tuples read the model, so a new column cannot land in neither list silently -- the same move rule 8 records as the fix for dbcore.WRITABLE_TABLES, and validate_pydantic_schemas already walks model-against-table so the drift gate comes free. (2) evidence_sources.jurisdiction has NO CHECK constraint, so widening who may amend it widened write access to a column whose vocabulary is not in the column; validate_jurisdiction is an after-the-fact scan, not a write-time gate, and the comment added this session overstates it. Fix: a migration adding the CHECK mirroring schemas/enums.py JurisdictionCode, after which dbcore.check_values supplies the vocabulary to every reader. (3) source_slug_links has nowhere to DECLARE a slug's local_ref_id label scheme, so _next_local_ref_id infers it per call and the mixed-scheme case can only refuse. Fix: slugs.local_ref_prefix (+ width) with a CHECK, which also subsumes GAP-285's missing UNIQUE(slug, local_ref_id) -- source_slug_links_duplicates.py reports duplicated labels under one slug today. (4) The relevance_note backfill path lives inside a create verb and is the THIRD hand-written amend mechanism (amend_source, amend_extraction, this), each with its own argument names and none sharing a ledger. Fix: one amend(table, key, field, value, reason) whose amendable set is derived per table, per (1). ALSO OWED: walk.py is cited by a checked-in workplan as its rule-7a generator but lives under scratchpad/, which schema_reference_audit SKIPs and derived_not_curated_audit's WRITER_ROOTS excludes -- it names ~30 tables and columns in raw SQL, so a rename sweeps every other reader and leaves it silently broken, which is rule 4's exact failure mode. It was NOT moved to scripts/ here because an unregistered executable under scripts/ is itself the defect rule 8 names; the move and the check-registry entry are one job, not two.
===== GAP-042
FOUR MORE evidence_sources VOCABULARIES LIVE ONLY IN A TEST FILE, AND THE WRITER CANNOT SEE ANY OF THEM. Migration 089 fixed the fifth. Derive the live state rather than trusting this list: python3 -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'scripts');import sqlite3,dbcore;con=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);print({c:sorted(dbcore.check_values(con,'evidence_sources',c)) for c in ('source_type','url_resolution_outcome','doi_resolution_outcome','metadata_quality','verification_status')})" -- measured 2026-09-20, source_type returns 17 values and the other four return the empty set, which dbcore.check_values' own docstring warns every caller reads as NO CONSTRAINT. THE TUPLES: VALID_VSTATUS, VALID_MQ, VALID_DOI_OUT and VALID_URL_OUT in scripts/tests/test_db_integrity.py, asserted by B01-B04. Each is CLAUDE.md rule 8's named anti-pattern -- a list maintained alongside the thing it describes, where the list and the thing drift and only the list is checked. WHY THIS IS NOT THEORETICAL, AND THE PROOF IS THIS BATCH. source_type was the fifth such tuple and it failed in the exact way rule 8 predicts: because the column declared no CHECK, db.py could not read the vocabulary, its --help advertised Crossref's 'journal-article' where the project's value is 'journal_article', a session copied the hyphen out of the help into the database, and B05 caught it two steps after argparse could have refused it for free. THE FOUR REMAINING COLUMNS ARE ONE add-source FLAG EACH, so the same path is open on all of them today. WHAT THE FIX LOOKS LIKE, already demonstrated: migration 089 rebuilt the table with the vocabulary in the column's own CHECK, B05 was rewritten to read dbcore.check_expression the way B06 reads it for gaps.status, and the flag was given choices=dbcore.schema_choices(...) so argparse refuses a bad value before the command runs and --help renders the live set. Three consumers, one home, nothing to keep in sync. WHY IT WAS NOT DONE FOR ALL FIVE AT ONCE: evidence_sources has 97 columns, 15 incoming foreign keys and 5 dependent views, so each CHECK costs a full table rebuild, and this batch did one to fix the defect it had actually caused rather than four more on spec. Doing the remaining four in ONE migration is cheaper than four -- one rebuild can add all four CHECKs. NOT A BACKLOG ITEM TO AGE: the next session that admits a source can hit this on any of the four, and the failure is silent at write time.

        # candidate's exec_id against the exec that actually admitted its source. The
        # tail still names it too -- that is the human-readable record, not the edge.

                     "resolved_ref_id=COALESCE(?, resolved_ref_id) "
                     "WHERE candidate_id=?",

    guess left legible beside the correction. These fields hold a WARRANT -- the

**The failure was three mechanisms deep, and only the third caught it:**

1.  **accepted** the bad value. Every other vocabulary flag on that
   command validates against the live schema; that guard was silently off here because an
   undeclared vocabulary reads as *no constraint*.
2.  **advertised** the value the blocking check rejects.
3. B05 caught it, from the curated tuple, two steps after argparse could have refused it
   for free.

**Migration 089** puts the vocabulary in the column's own CHECK — the ratified answer, per
CLAUDE.md §4 ("vocabularies come from the schema, not a list in code"). Deliberately **not**
a  enum in : that would move the list, not remove it, and
leave two homes where rule 5 allows one.

Three consumers now derive from that one declaration:

-  takes , so **argparse refuses the typo
  before the command runs** and names the live set.
-  renders the vocabulary instead of restating it, so it cannot drift again.
- **B05 reads ** and the tuple is gone.  75/75.

**The DDL was generated from the live schema, not retyped.**  has 97
columns; hand-transcribing them to add one constraint would have been the same class of
error the migration exists to fix. **The first attempt failed and is worth recording:**
SQLite validates the whole schema during , so the five dependent
views aborted it with *"error in view v_evidence_authors: no such table"*. It rolled back
atomically and left the blob untouched — 's transaction boundary (DR-2026-08-19
F5) doing its job. The migration drops and restores those views verbatim.

 reproduces the result, which is the check that matters for a table
rebuild.

**GAP-042 records what this did not do.** Four sibling vocabularies on the same table —
, , , 
— are still curated tuples over columns that declare nothing, and each is one 
flag away from the identical failure. They were left because each CHECK costs a full rebuild
of a 97-column table and this batch did one to fix the defect it had actually caused, not
four more on spec. The gap notes that all four fit in **one** rebuild.

## 11. Gates

- `research_batch_dod --session` — **COMPLIANT, 19/19.** R1 and R7 failed first and were remediated
  by a real Co-1 pass and real candidate staging, not by waiver.
- `run_checks.py --changed-from origin/main` — **PASS.** Re-derive the counts.
- `run_checks.py --selftest` — **PASS.**
- `retrieval_log --verify-authors` — clean for this batch's one admission. 26 of 27 sources have no
  logged retrieval and are not verifiable offline: a corpus-wide condition this batch neither caused
  nor fixed.
- Derived outputs regenerated and `--check`-clean; context map regenerated.

## 12. The determination did not move, exactly as predicted

**Parameter 3 × MOB stays undetermined. Determination gate 1 stays open. `specifications` gains no
live row.** Prior P4 put this at 0.95 and gave the reason: the blocker is C10 over REF-01002's
UNVERIFIED status, which nothing in this assignment touches, and both retrieval targets are pre-1990
and therefore historical grounding under the owner ruling of 2026-09-18. **Retrieving both in full
would still leave the cell undetermined.** That is the batch's expected outcome, not a shortfall.

## 13. What the next batch takes

1. **The accessibility-audit cluster, and it is the cheapest real evidence in view.** REF-01006's
   references hold at least five audits of real health facilities — Pinto 2021 (Brazil, national,
   doi 10.3390/ijerph18062953), Garg 2024 (doi 10.1016/j.mjafi.2022.10.011), Singh 2024 (New Delhi),

   the opposite direction. They are DOI-bearing and open access, so unlike everything this batch
   chased they are actually retrievable here.
2. **Templer 1978, one retrieval and no more** (candidate 117). NBS is now NIST and its internal

3. **Walter 1971 and Elmer 1957 go to document delivery, not to a fourth retrieval ladder** —

4. **Confirm or refute the footnote-c scope** (§3) against a cleaner scan of page 57. It is one look

5. **GAP-016 stays open and is not a search.**

**Not attempted, and owed a third batch running:** GAP-033 — term adjudication has never run.

def fetch(url, session, purpose="", timeout=40, stamp=None, ref_id=None):
    """Retrieve a URL, PERSIST the raw response, then return the parsed JSON.

    The write happens before the return, deliberately: the artefact on disk is the
    bytes the caller actually received, not a later re-fetch that may differ.

    Returns None on ANY failure: curl itself failing (no HTTP response at all), an
    empty body, a body that is not JSON -- OR, as of 2026-09-13, an HTTP status
    outside 2xx. The artefact and the manifest line are written regardless: a
    failed retrieval is still evidence of what was attempted and what came back,
    and CLAUDE.md 5(c) is exactly the case for keeping it (see `status` below).
    """
    # BYTES, NOT TEXT, AND FOLLOW REDIRECTS. Both fixed 2026-09-02 after measurement.
    #
    # This function's docstring promises "the artefact on disk is the bytes the caller
    # actually received". With `text=True` that promise was FALSE for every non-UTF-8
    # body, and false SILENTLY -- no exception, exit code 0. curl decoded the bytes with
    # replacement characters, `body.encode("utf-8")` re-encoded the damaged text, and the
    # manifest recorded a sha256 of the damage. Measured on a real RCOT PDF: stored
    # bdfeba45..., actually received ab78cbbc... . A logger whose hash does not identify
    # what arrived cannot support the fidelity audit it exists for, and PDF is the format
    # Co-1 and disability-led evidence overwhelmingly arrives in.
    #
    # `-L` because a DOI is a 302. Without it the artefact was the redirect stub: one
    # 0-byte figshare line sits in this session's manifest as evidence of exactly that.
    #
    # This is the ROOT CAUSE of D04-032, which was closed on 2026-09-02 by reconstructing
    # a manifest for 58 unlogged payloads. That fix treated the symptom -- it never asked
    # why the payloads were unlogged. This is why.
    #
    # HTTP STATUS, NOT JUST EXIT CODE. Fixed 2026-09-13. `curl` without `--fail` exits 0
    # for ANY completed HTTP transaction, 404 and publisher interstitial included -- the
    # body it hands back is an error page, and until now the manifest recorded that as a
    # successful retrieval indistinguishable from the real thing. `-o <tempfile> -w
    # '%{http_code}'` sends the body straight to disk untouched and returns ONLY the
    # final status code (final, because of `-L`: the code after redirects are followed,
    # which is the code for the bytes actually stored) on stdout -- so the body is never
    # routed through Python at all before being read back as bytes, and the "capture
    # bytes exactly" promise above is unaffected by this change; it is the same promise,
    # applied one file-write earlier. A transport failure that never got an HTTP response
    # (DNS, TLS, timeout before headers) reports "000" from curl, which is not a status
    # and is stored as `status: null` rather than invented as 0 or 200.
    fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix="retrieval-log-", suffix=".tmp")
    os.close(fd)
    tmp = Path(tmp_path)
    try:
        # CONTENT TYPE IS CAPTURED, added 2026-09-17, and the charset inside it is the
        # reason. The server's `Content-Type: text/html; charset=Shift_JIS` is the ONLY
        # authoritative statement of how these bytes decode, and it was being thrown away
        # at the one moment it exists. Everything downstream then assumed UTF-8, so a
        # Japanese, Chinese, Korean or Arabic page served in a legacy encoding became
        # mojibake in the verifier while its sha256 stayed perfectly valid. Two fields on
        # one -w is a tab-separated line, parsed below.
        r = subprocess.run(
            ["curl", "-sS", "-L", "--max-time", str(timeout),
             "-o", str(tmp), "-w", "%{http_code}\t%{content_type}", url],
            capture_output=True)
        body = tmp.read_bytes() if tmp.exists() else b""  # bytes, straight off disk
    finally:
        tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    raw_w = r.stdout.decode("ascii", errors="replace").strip()
    code_raw, _, content_type = raw_w.partition("\t")
    code_raw = code_raw.strip()
    content_type = content_type.strip() or None
    # curl's own sentinel for "no HTTP response was ever received" is the literal
    # string "000" (measured: a proxy CONNECT failure prints it, curl exit 56).
    # That is not a status code -- 0 is not in any HTTP spec -- so it is None, the
    # same as a stdout curl could not produce a code for at all.
    status = (int(code_raw) if code_raw.isdigit() and len(code_raw) == 3
               and code_raw != "000" else None)
    d = LOG_ROOT / _session_stem(session)
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    sha = hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()  # of what arrived, not of a lossy decode
    artefact = f"{sha[:16]}{_extension_for(body)}"
    (d / artefact).write_bytes(body)
    with open(d / "manifest.jsonl", "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write(json.dumps({
            "retrieved_at": stamp or _now(), "url": url, "purpose": purpose,
            # STRUCTURED ref_id, added 2026-09-13. Every ref_id the manifest carried
            # before this was free text inside `purpose`, so nothing downstream could
            # scope a quote check to the source it is attributed to -- and
            # `quote_in_artefacts` below says exactly that residual out loud rather
            # than pretending a corpus-wide byte match proves attribution.
            "ref_id": ref_id,
            "sha256": sha, "bytes": len(body), "exit": r.returncode,
            "status": status, "artefact": artefact,
            # The server's own statement of how to decode these bytes. Null for every
            # artefact retrieved before 2026-09-17, which is why _decode_artefact()
            # below must still work from the bytes alone.
            "content_type": content_type,
        }, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    if r.returncode != 0 or not body.strip():
        return None
    if status is None or not (200 <= status < 300):
        return None                        # HTTP-layer failure: recorded above, not hidden
    try:
        # Decode ONLY to parse, never to store. A binary body simply is not JSON, and
        # `errors="replace"` keeps that a clean None rather than an exception raised
        # after the artefact is already safely on disk.
        return json.loads(body.decode("utf-8", errors="replace"))
    except Exception:
        return None

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
scripts/audit/derived_not_curated_audit.py — CLAUDE.md rule 8, mechanised.

THE RULE: derive it, or name who judged it. Never curate a fact the machine can compute.

WHAT WRONG THING REACHES THE GUIDEBOOK WITHOUT THIS. A curated list and the thing it
describes drift, and only the list is ever read. Every instance found on 2026-09-13 failed
in the SAFE-LOOKING direction, which is why none was noticed:

  * `dbcore.WRITABLE_TABLES` — a hand list of the tables a session may write. Blind eight
    times. A `gap_mining` row written through the sanctioned CLI was captured as nothing
    and the session was told "no delta — nothing to emit".
  * `db.py --verification-method` — an argparse `choices=` list missing `direct-render`
    for as long as that value had existed, so the CLI REFUSED a value the schema admits.
  * `PRE_075_UNGRADED_IDS` — a frozen id list that outlived the rows it froze.
  * `governance/check-registry.yaml`'s "N today" counts — every one measured stale.

None of those made a wrong claim reach the book directly. Each made a TRUE thing
unreachable, or a checkable thing uncheckable, which is how a corpus quietly stops being
verifiable.

WHAT THIS CHECKS, and why only this class for now. Rule 8 is general and most of it is
judgement, which a script cannot police. ONE class of violation is mechanically decidable:
an argparse `choices=` literal whose values are exactly a live column's CHECK vocabulary.
That is a second home with a first home sitting next to it, and the fix is always the same
(`dbcore.schema_choices(table, column)`). The other known violations named in rule 8 —
`--ref-id` and `--tier` asking for derivable values, the curated `MODEL_TABLE_MAP`, the
registry's counts — need judgement about what the single home should BE, so they are
listed in the rule for a reader rather than asserted here.

A SECOND MECHANICALLY DECIDABLE CLASS, added 2026-09-17: A WRITER THAT NAMES A COLUMN
THE LIVE SCHEMA DOES NOT HAVE. A row dict spelling its own audit columns as string
literals is the same defect as a curated vocabulary -- a second home for the column's
name, with the first home (the schema) sitting right there.

  Migration 085 renamed `search_executions.session` -> `created_by_session` and

# ALTITUDE review — batch 19 infrastructure diff

Ten findings, ordered by how much depth is missing. Line numbers are working-tree lines. I edited nothing.

---

## 1. `scripts/db.py:3872` (`_AMENDABLE`) and `:6217` (`_AMENDABLE_SVE_FIELDS`) — growing the list is the wrong altitude; amendability should be derived by complement

**Measured:** `evidence_sources` has 97 columns. 12 are amendable, 8 correctable, **77 are in neither list and are therefore silently unrepairable**. The list's growth cadence *is* the defect signature: `verification_disposition` (09-02), `jurisdiction` (09-18), `verification_status` + `doi_resolution_outcome` (09-18), `source_type` (09-20) — five additions in eighteen days, every one provoked by a row that had **already** been written wrong and had cost a compensating migration. GAP-013 named this in the abstract; this diff is the fifth instance, and it grows the list twice (`source_type`; `root_type` + `root_ref_id`).

**Deeper change I would make:** invert the default. `dbcore.amendable(conn, table)` = live columns from `PRAGMA table_info` − `_CORRECTABLE` keys − a **named exclusion set** (`ref_id`, `created_*`/`updated_*`, the migration-063 author tombstones, anything a view computes), each exclusion carrying its one-line reason. That is verbatim the move rule 8 records as the fix for `dbcore.WRITABLE_TABLES` — *"it is now derived, and the burden of proof moved to the exclusions."* Safety does not live in the membership tuple: it lives in `check_declared`, the ledger, and the specific I4-style refusals, all of which are per-field and all of which stay.

One correction to GAP-013's own proposed fix: `schemas/evidence_source.py` mirrors roughly twenty of the 97 columns, so `json_schema_extra={'provenance': ...}` cannot be the home today without first completing the model. The complement-of-`_CORRECTABLE` derivation needs no new metadata and can land now.

## 2. `scripts/db.py:3497` + `scripts/research/retrieval_log.py:533` — the payload→column map now has two identical homes, and this diff writes the same two lambdas into both

`_CORRECTABLE`'s header states the invariant in its own words: the correctable set is *"EXACTLY what retrieval_log --verify-authors can prove against a payload."* The diff's new comment in `retrieval_log` records that invariant being broken hours earlier (`journal_name`/`publisher` added to one side only). The repair is **to copy the same lambdas into the other side** — including a byte-identical `next((t for t in (m.get("container-title") or []) if t), None)` in two files. `db.py:3526` already does `import retrieval_log` inside the very function that consumes `_CORRECTABLE`.

**Deeper change:** one map in `retrieval_log` (`PAYLOAD_FIELDS`); `_BIBLIO_FIELDS = PAYLOAD_FIELDS`; `_CORRECTABLE = dict(PAYLOAD_FIELDS)` plus `pub_title` (which the verifier handles through `_TITLE_COLS` — make that exception explicit rather than implicit). The stated invariant then holds by construction instead of by comment, and rule 5 stops being broken in the code that enforces rule 5 in the data.

## 3. `scripts/migrations/089_source_type_vocabulary.sql:70` — one CHECK inside a rebuild that had already paid for five

The proportionality argument in the session record does not hold, and GAP-042's own text says so. The cost of 089 is the 97-column rebuild, the drop-and-restore of five dependent views, the `AFTER_DATA` boundary and a new binary DB blob — not the CHECK clause. The DDL was *generated* from the live schema, so four more constraints are four more generated lines in a file that is already 539 lines. Against that, a second rebuild later is a second chance to lose a view (the first attempt of *this* migration already aborted on exactly that), a second data boundary, and a second binary conflict for every open PR touching the DB when the scheduled `source-verification` run fires (CLAUDE.md rule 3). GAP-042 itself: *"Doing the remaining four in ONE migration is cheaper than four"* and *"NOT A BACKLOG ITEM TO AGE."*

**Deeper change:** 089 carries all five CHECKs. And one level up, the recurring mechanism — *a vocabulary that lives only in a test tuple over a column that declares nothing* — has no detector, which GAP-038 already records (*"nothing DETECTS the class"*). Extend `scripts/audit/derived_not_curated_audit.py` with a third mechanically decidable class: **a module-level literal collection whose members are all values of, or all column names of, one live table's column that declares no CHECK.** That file already argues its two existing classes exactly this way, and this third class would have listed all five columns on 2026-09-18 instead of letting a session trip over the fifth.

## 4. `scripts/research/mining_screen.py:54, 172, 247` — the floor/ceiling band is the artefact of the shallow fix and should be deleted, not repaired

**Measured now, on the live log:** `python3 scripts/research/mining_screen.py` prints **no band on any row** — twelve anchors, every cell a point. The only `ocr_damaged` payload is `08263082ebdda8eb.json`, which the *same diff's* supersession logic deliberately drops, and the corrected READ transcription carries no `inferred` key at all. So `score_ceiling()`, the `reading` parameter, the two-transcription entry shape and a third of the printed footer are exercised by nothing in the repository.

The session record diagnoses this itself — *"the band was measuring the distance between a bad text layer and my own guesses"* — and then the review pass spent a cycle fixing a bug **inside** the band (ceiling could fall below floor) rather than removing it. §8 puts the burden of proof on keeping apparatus, not on deleting it.

**Deeper change:** delete `score_ceiling`, the `reading` argument, and the `inferred` reading concept. **Keep** the three-way provenance label — it is cheap and stops a scraped list reading as the publisher's own. Then make the tool **refuse** to score a `SCRAPED` list: *"this list came off a damaged text layer; re-transcribe from `page_image.py` renders first."* One refusal replaces a measurement apparatus, and it is the doctrine `db.py` is built on (*"db.py refuses, and that is its whole value"*).

Secondary, same file: `DERIVED_ARTEFACTS` at `:36` is a module-level dict filled as a side effect of `payloads_by_ref()`, and `provenance_of()` silently falls back to re-parsing the body when it is empty — an implicit call-order dependency, plus up to two re-reads of the same file. `payloads_by_ref()` should return records (path **and** its manifest line) and `provenance_of` should be a pure function of a record.

## 5. `scripts/research/retrieval_log.py:305` and `:363` — three writers of a manifest line; one concept with three entry points

`fetch`, `derive` and `record_file` each hand-assemble the same JSON dict, hash separately, and construct the `derived:` URI separately.
